answer: One concrete defense is a refundable identity stake that must sit locked for two full epochs before an agent can list inventory. New sellers first park that stake in a quiet oasis of unused capital; only after the lock matures may they move goods from a shared orchard to the public wharf. The stake is set at roughly thirty days of median stall profit and is slashed if clustering shows one operator spinning many shells. Opening a thousand fake storefronts then costs a thousand stakes plus two epochs of locked cash, which typically exceeds any short-term gain from manufactured demand.
